Shown below in [fig-3d-basis] are the vectors $\evec_1$, $\evec_2$, and $\evec_3$ in $\real^3$.

The vectors $\evec_1$, $\evec_2$, and $\evec_3$ in $\real^3$.

Imagine that the thumb of your right hand points in the direction of $\evec_1$. A positive rotation about the $x$ axis corresponds to a rotation in the direction in which your fingers point. Find the matrix definining the matrix transformation $T$ that rotates vectors by $90^\circ$ around the $x$-axis.

In the same way, find the matrix that rotates vectors by $90^\circ$ around the $y$-axis.

Find the matrix that rotates vectors by $90^\circ$ around the $z$-axis.

What is the cumulative effect of rotating by $90^\circ$ about the $x$-axis, followed by a $90^\circ$ rotation about the $y$-axis, followed by a $-90^\circ$ rotation about the $x$-axis.
